findings.text: follow-on: the guard the node added to _REFUSAL_FOR_PATH covers only the machine-readable op objects _documented_op_objects extracts, so reinstating the retired PROSE instructions -- the coordinator-reference.md:135 form `ops=[set status + resolve driving followup + append next followup] (mutated)`, an `ops=[set status ...]` phrase, or an `outcome: "done - no followup"` recipe -- into any of the four other files would not redden any test; the five-file grep in the run's log is a one-off measurement, not a standing guard, so a later prose regression is caught by review rather than by the suite.

justifications.durability: the added assertion is independent of its input -- tests/test_skill_contracts.py:2033 extends _REFUSAL_FOR_PATH so a terminal-status refusal counts as a refusal for the op's path, and the op objects are read from the skills docs while the refusal comes from reckon/_store.py:2577, so reinstating the archive example's terminal set reddens test_every_documented_op_object_is_supported_by_the_store, exactly as logs/negative-control.log shows; the gap that keeps this below full is that the extractor (_documented_op_objects, tests/test_skill_contracts.py:2102) reads only JSON op objects, so the prose forms the node also retired are guarded by no test.
justifications.evidence: the gate measure is recorded and not merely claimed (logs/head.log and logs/baseline.log each end 74 passed / EXIT=0 at their revisions, and the manifest's after_suite revision equals head.log's first line), the negative-control red log carries the store's own refusal text and the one failing id the head arm does not fail, and I re-ran the grep arm independently at both trees (0 hits at 20b6e6b56, 8 at 2cbe964ac) rather than taking the log on trust.
justifications.fit: the doc edits keep the surrounding markdown idiom (the close row mirrors the existing op-table rows, and the four prose sites are edited in place), the fragment's element ids all carry the node-id prefix the dispatch requires, and the diff introduces no plan, sprint or ticket label into code, symbols or filenames.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the op table's new close row (skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:394) matches reckon/_store.py:3290 _apply_close exactly (terminal status, non-empty outcome, by, optional superseded_by) and every positive instruction to set a terminal plan status is gone from the five files (0 hits at 20b6e6b56 vs 8 at 2cbe964ac), the only remaining skills-tree terminal `set` being skills/reckon-sprint/SKILL.md:188 against a sprint resource, which reckon/_store.py:2572-2577 does not refuse because the guard is gated on type == 'plan'.
justifications.reuse: the node adds no capability: it documents the close op that reckon/_store.py:3290 already owns and extends the existing harness predicate at tests/test_skill_contracts.py:2029 by one alternative rather than introducing a parallel refusal classifier, so nothing is forked.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff (six files in 1161f3735 plus the fragment in 20b6e6b56) is inside the node's eight declared write paths, no figure was written though docs/figures/... was granted, and the change carries nothing the goal does not imply.
